headline_marked: [[No Man's Sky launches on iPhone and iPad]] with all decade-long updates, free to try
headline: No Man's Sky launches on iPhone and iPad with all decade-long updates, free to try
summary: The acclaimed space exploration game, along with Sifu and other indie titles, is now available for pre-order or download, taking less than 5GB and supporting older iOS devices.
details: No Man's Sky is now available for pre-order on iPhone and iPad, with an official release date of October 28. The mobile version will be free to try and includes all updates from the past decade, requiring less than 5GB of storage.

Hello Games has rebuilt touch controls for the iOS port, which also supports TV casting, controller inputs, and mouse and keyboard on iPad. The game is optimized to be playable on devices as old as iPhone 11 and 3rd generation iPad Air.

Initially, the iOS and iPadOS versions will not include multiplayer or settlements, mirroring the initial launch restrictions of the Nintendo Switch port. Hello Games plans to add these features based on player feedback and numbers, similar to their support for the Switch.

Apple's Indie Games Week also highlights other notable titles arriving on iOS, including the challenging martial arts beat-'em-up Sifu. Sifu's iOS version features a reworked camera system and optimized touch controls.

Other indie games launching include Vampire Crawlers, a strategic card-based game, and Dome Keeper, a roguelite blending mining and tower defense. Yes, Your Grace 2: Snowfall, 9 Kings, and Little Kitty, Big City are also available now.

Carson Oliver, Apple's head of App Store Worldwide, emphasized the App Store's role in showcasing indie developers' creativity. The event celebrates teams taking creative risks to push gaming forward on Apple platforms.
